## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle Eastern-Hàn Buddha-biography sūtra recounting the lineage and youth of the future Buddha — his Tuṣita-heaven previous life, his descent, his birth in Kapilavastu, and the early phases of his renunciation. Translated jointly by [竺大力](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E5%A4%A7%E5%8A%9B) Mahābala (Indian *śramaṇa*) and [康孟詳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%B7%E5%AD%9F%E8%A9%B3) Kāng Mèngxiáng (Hàn-Chinese collaborator) in the late Eastern Hàn. Signature: 「後漢西域三藏竺大力共康孟詳譯」.

T184 is one of the earliest stand-alone Buddha-biography texts in Chinese — a foundational document of the Hàn-period reception of Buddhist hagiography — and the source-text for many later sinophone Buddha-biography elaborations.

**Abstract**

T184's translation is documented in the *Chū sānzàng jì jí* 出三藏記集 ([KR6s0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0084)) to Jiàn'ān 建安 2 = 197 CE — one of the most precisely-dated Hàn-period translations after [安世高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96%E9%AB%98) Ān Shìgāo's. The Indic source corresponds to a *Lalitavistara*-class Buddha-biography in early-Mahāyāna form, though no exact Indic recension can be identified. The work is paired with *[Zhōng běnqǐ jīng (T196)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0053)* — translated jointly by [曇果](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E6%9E%9C) Tánguǒ and Kāng Mèngxiáng — which continues the Buddha-biography from the *bodhi*-tree onward; the two texts together constitute a complete Buddha-biography cycle in the Eastern-Hàn Chinese tradition.

The *Buddha-biography* genre played a foundational role in the Hàn-period sinophone formation of Buddhism: T184 and T196 together gave the Chinese reading public their first sustained narrative encounter with the life of the Buddha, and provided the imaginative-doctrinal framework within which Mahāyāna *bodhisattva*-doctrine and later *Buddhāvataṃsaka*-class scriptures could be received.
